segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And while Julian was riding about,
and urging on the battle,
and boasting in his good fortune,
suddenly an arrow flew and struck him in his side;
and when he fell, he died.
It is said
that he filled his hands with his blood and cast it toward heaven, saying:
"You have conquered me, Jesus {OCR: [Ye]shua} the Galilean!
Acknowledge henceforth, along with divinity, also kingship."
And to one of the holy men it was shown in a vision
that one of the forty holy martyrs had shot the arrow.
When Julian died,
and the Roman army was defeated, especially by famine,
because Shapur had seized the approaches for provisions,
they then sought a king for themselves,
and they chose Jovian the believer, who was a chiliarch.
He, however, swore,
"I will not become a king over pagans."
Then they all cried out,
"We are all Christians!"
And tears were mingled with joy.
And they set up a cross in the midst,
and upon its top a crown.
And when they had knelt and worshipped the cross,
they took the crown and placed it upon the head of Jovian.
And he, in his humility, went to Shapur.
And when Shapur said
that until the Romans gave up to the Persians as far as the Euphrates,
the slaughter that had occurred among them would not be avenged,
he gave him Nisibis alone without its people {OCR?}, and appeased him.
And he made peace for thirty years.
And both sides rejoiced,
and the camps mingled with one another.
And he also showed care for Julian,
and carried him up with him in a coffin,
and buried him in Tarsus,
as Socrates says;
and afterwards he was transferred to Constantinople.
And because of this, Themistius the philosopher blamed the people of his generation,
because they did not honor God, but the purple, and served {OCR: and honored?} it. Jovian, however, when he returned from Persia, passed through Cilicia,
and reached the Bosporus {OCR?}, in a village named Dadastana {OCR?}, on the border of Bithynia and Galatia;
he fell ill with a disease of the kidneys in the wintertime, and died there.
Valentinian {OCR?} and Valens {OCR?}, brothers, thirteen years.
This one was from the country of Pannonia, from the city of Cibalae.
